top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock meets the tests I apply to any instrument: a clear original idea (magic-wavelength trapping, Katori), a long programme of systematics control to 10^-18 (Ye and JILA), independent reproduction and clock-to-clock agreement at several laboratories, and physics already delivered (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, a many-body clock regime, limits on varying constants and ultralight dark matter). The two-name allocation follows the two decisive steps, and the citation can state both the invention and the achieved precision, which separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. It is mature enough that no award would be a worse outcome.
